rationale: A wins because it keeps the story inside the evidence and makes the missing proof do actual work. Its strongest line, "Allbirds' first margin gain isn't enough to erase its IPO-day math," is a clean reporter-shaped tension: margin moved, losses remain. B has sharper theater, but "Allbirds Quietly Dropped 'Eco-Friendly' as Its Main Pitch" asserts a marketing pivot the update does not prove. That is how a decent angle becomes a fact-check problem with nicer shoes.
gaps_in_A: "Allbirds swaps wool for a sugarcane blend" slightly muddies the material fact; the update says a sugarcane-and-wool blend, not a clean swap away from wool.
"DTC brands are shrinking to survive" is plausible, but it needs comparables before it can stand as more than Allbirds plus a trend costume.
"finally make its shoes last" overstates the durability fact; the update only says Allbirds claims the new blend is more durable than the original wool runner.
gaps_in_B: "Allbirds Quietly Dropped 'Eco-Friendly' as Its Main Pitch" is not in the update. B asks for proof later, but the headline has already spent a fact it does not have.
"For a Brand Built on Cutting Out Middlemen, That's a Concession" imports a brand-origin thesis and value judgment not supplied in the facts.
"the wreckage of the 2021 D2C IPO cohort" may be a smart frame, but it is outside the provided update and needs sourcing before it belongs in an angle set.
"meanest-editor" as the next step is the wrong move; the blocker is partner identity and hard proof, not another roast.
